research_question: In older adults (≥55 years) with an anxiety or related disorder, what is the effect of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) compared with minimal management on dropout rates at 3–6 months post-treatment?
control_label: Minimal management (waitlist, usual care, supportive/attention control, or medication alone)
outcome_description: Cumulative participant dropout/discontinuation rate at 3–6 months post-treatment follow-up (number of participants dropping out or lost to follow-up relative to total randomized per arm)
positive_direction: A risk ratio greater than 1.0 indicates a higher rate of dropout in the CBT group compared with the minimal management control group
search_queries: cognitive behavioral therapy older adults anxiety randomized controlled trial
CBT late life anxiety follow up trial attrition
cognitive therapy elderly anxiety disorder controlled trial dropout
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials comparing cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) to minimal management (waitlist, treatment-as-usual, attention control, or medication without active psychotherapy) in older adults (≥55 years) with an anxiety or related disorder
Reports quantitative dropout, discontinuation, or retention data at 3–6 months post-treatment follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomized controlled trial (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, study protocols, editorials, and non-RCT designs are excluded)
No comparison between CBT and an eligible minimal management control condition (e.g., comparisons solely against another active psychological therapy)
No quantitative data on participant dropout or discontinuation at 3–6 months post-treatment
Population not comprised of older adults (age <55 years) or not diagnosed with an anxiety or related disorder
moderators_to_extract: Type of minimal management control (waitlist, usual care, attention/supportive control, medication)
Follow-up timing within window (3 months vs. 6 months post-treatment)
Specific anxiety disorder diagnosis (e.g., GAD, panic, mixed anxiety)
effect_size_note: Risk Ratio (RR) calculated from cumulative dropout events and total randomized participants per arm. If sequential dropouts are reported across phases, they are summed to obtain cumulative dropout by 3-6 months post-treatment. If multiple follow-up timepoints exist between 3 and 6 months, the latest follow-up within this window is used.
